_readme: Preview scene fixups. See ldd-lili-collection.json for the format.

_why: The Bound Arrow card drew a hard-edged violet slab with the arrow
buried inside it (field 2026-08-21, twice). The slab is FlamesMesh02:
a glow plane carrying a LIGHTING shader and, in the copy this load
order actually loads, NO NiAlphaProperty at all. Nothing marks it as
transparent, so the pass drew it opaque and its quad edges are the
sharp rectangle.
A code rule was tried first and was wrong: skipping geometry whose
blend modes the pass cannot reproduce. ENB Light re-authors the ARROW
ITSELF as blend on, srcAlpha to ONE, alpha test GREATER 128, so that
rule ate Arrow1 through Arrow6 and Arrow:0 while leaving the slab
untouched, because a shape with no alpha property has no blend modes
to judge. It was reverted. The lesson is in the tracker as OS-244.
Censused with tools/nif_shape_alpha.py over every bound weapon mesh
in the load order (ENB Light, ENB Light - Misc Effects, Remove Arrow
and Bolt Trail VFX; ElSopa and LeanWolf ship none). The FX families
are named consistently across all of them: FlamesMesh, FlamesMesh01,
FlamesMesh02, FlamesHit01..04, RefractMesh2, RefractMesh03,
RefrectHit01, RefrectHit02 (the author's own spelling), ENBLight01,
trailShort and Flow:0. The real pieces are Arrow1..Arrow6, Arrow:0,
ArrowQuiver:0 and BoundArrowFlight:0, and not one of them contains
any of those tokens. That is checkable because this family was
censused whole, which is why the rule is scoped to this path rather
than added to the global helper tokens.
⚠ The *encheffects.nif meshes in this folder are FX end to end and
would be hidden entirely by these patterns. They are enchantment
effect meshes rather than item models, so nothing builds a card from
one; if that ever changes, this scope has to narrow to the arrow.
A scope tag re-keys exactly the cards it covers, which is also what
clears the slab already sitting in the PNG cache.
